title: Restricted conjunction of DNFs has a low-width simple CNF
statement: Let $g_1,\dots,g_s$ be DNF formulas in $n$ Boolean variables, and let $f : (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}) \to \mathrm{Bool}$ be their conjunction, so that $f(x) = \mathrm{true}$ if and only if $g_i(x) = \mathrm{true}$ for every $i$. Fix a restriction $\rho$ of the $n$ variables, and write $h_\rho$ for the restriction of a Boolean function $h$ by $\rho$ (the function obtained by fixing each coordinate that $\rho$ sets and leaving the rest free). Suppose that for every $i$ the restricted gate $(g_i)_\rho$ has decision-tree depth at most $l$. Then the restricted function $f_\rho$ is computed by some CNF formula $\Psi$ of width at most $l$ — every clause contains at most $l$ literals — in which each clause is simple: no literal occurs twice, and any two literals in a clause that share a variable are identical. That is, $\Psi(x) = f_\rho(x)$ for all $x$.
hypotheses_covered: f is the conjunction of the DNF gates g_1,...,g_s (f(x) true iff every gate is true at x)
rho is a restriction of the n variables
each restricted gate (g_i)_rho has decision-tree depth at most l
replaced:
Suppose $f$ is the AND of the gates ($f(x) = \mathrm{true}$ iff every gate is true at
$x$) and each restricted gate has decision-tree depth $\le l$. Then there is a CNF
$\Psi$ of width $\le l$, with nodup and variable-injective clauses, whose evaluation
equals $\mathrm{restrictFn}\, f\,\rho_1$.
